This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court   following:
JUDGEMENT
With the consent of the parties, the matter is finally heard.

The appellant/claimant has filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act (in short "the Act") assailing the award passed by the learned IIIrd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Rewa, in MACC No.1900219/2015 on 26/11/2021, whereby claim petition has been partly allowed and award for Rs.9,74,632/- along with 7% interest from the date of filing of the claim petition i.e. 4/8/2015 has been passed.
2. Facts in brief giving rise to the claim case are that on 6/3/2014 the appellant with his wife was going from village Mangawan to Alamganj riding on his motorcycle bearing registration no.MP-17-MA- 0519.

entities.text: IIIrd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Rewa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
At about 6:00 p.m., as he reached near Shere Punjab Dhaba in village Ambi,
respondent no.1 driving tanker no. O.R.-14-T-5958 rashly and negligently came from Rewa side and going on wrong side hit motorcycle with extreme force which caused severe injuries to the appellant resulting in permanent disablement.

2.1 In claim petition it has also been narrated that before accident, the appellant was serving in Adult Education Department, working as Mate in village Panchayat and also performing agricultural activities.
He was earning Rs.3000/- from Adult Education Department, Rs.10,000/- p.m. from agricultural activities and Rs.4,050/- p.m. from village Panchayat.
Due to the permanent disablement caused by injuries sustained in the accident, he has lost his income and has also incurred near about Rs. 5,00,000/- on treatment.
Thus, claimant preferred the claim petition for amount of compensation of Rs.60,47,800/- with interest.

3. Respondents no.1 and 2 controverting the allegations of the claim petition specifically mentioned that on the date of accident, offending vehicle was insured with the insurance company/respondent no.3, therefore, if any liability of payment arises, that will be payable by the insurance company.

Respondent no.3/insurance company disputed the factum of income of the appellant of Rs.17,050/-
p.m. and also averred that driver of the offending vehicle was not having registration fitness permit and valid and effective license which is violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.

Hence,
insurance company is not liable to pay any amount of compensation.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant has taken exception to the impugned award; firstly, on the ground that income of the appellant should have been taken as Rs.5500/- p.m. as per guideline of M.P. State Legal Services Authority No.F.No.21/NLA/MPSLSA/24/7/2022, Jabalpur dated 28/7/2022 (for short "the guidelines of MPSLSA").

entities.text: M.P. State Legal Services Authority No.F.No.21/NLA/MPSLSA/24/7/2022, Jabalpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Secondly, he submits that in the head of future prospects 40% of the income should have been added as per the guidelines given in the judgment of Rajkumar Pandey vs Sanjay Kumar Singh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57453241/
2 National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 (16) SCC 680. Lastly, he has pointed out that even though disability certificate submitted by the appellant reveals permanent disability of 60% but the learned claims tribunal took the disability of the appellant only 40% ignoring the fact that functional disability of the appellant is 100%.

For this, he has drawn attention of this Court towards para 15 of the impugned award and also relied on the judgments of the Apex Court in Gurudev Singh vs. Reliance General Ins. Co., (2023)ACJ 1255, Jithendran vs. The New India Assurance Co. Limited and Another,(2021) ACJ 2736 and Sarnam Singh vs. Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd. and others, (2023) ACJ 1450.
5.

entities.text: Gurudev Singh vs. Reliance General Ins. Co., (2023)ACJ 1255
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Jithendran vs. The New India Assurance Co. Limited and Another,(2021) ACJ 2736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarnam Singh vs. Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd. and others, (2023) ACJ 1450
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent no.3/insurance company submits that appellant could not prove his income as claim in claim petition, therefore, the learned claims tribunal was not bound to take resort to the guidelines given by the MPSLSA for notional income.
He has also disputed that functional disability of the appellant is not upto 100%.
Learned claims tribunal has rightly taken disability to 40% and supporting the impugned award the counsel has prayed for dismissing this appeal as devoid of substance.

6. Heard rival contention raised by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
On the date of accident, appellant was of 36 years of age is not disputed.
From perusal of the disability certificate (Ex.P/13), it is found that disability has been assessed 60%.

This certificate has been issued by the office of Civil Surgeon cum Chief Superintendent, Rewa and has been proved by Dr. Sanjeev Shukla (PW/3), who was one of the expert members of the District Disablement Board.

Nothing adverse has emerged in cross examination of this witness, therefore, percentage of disability, as reduced by the learned claims tribunal in paragraph 17 of the impugned award to 40%,
is not sustainable.

This finding is set aside and it is held that disability caused by the injuries to the appellant is 60% as assessed by the Disablement Board, Rewa in disability certificate (Ex.P/13).
8.
Contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that functional disability is 100% is also not sustainable as only lower limbs of the appellant have been affected by the injuries.
Thus, contention in this regard being not based on any substantial evidence is repelled.
9. As far as the contention of the learned counsel for the respondent no.3/insurance company regarding grant of amount in the head of future prospect is concerned, it has force.
Learned claims tribunal has not awarded any amount in the above head and no reasons have been assigned there for.
10. It is undisputed that at the time of accident, the injured was 36 years of age and suffered permanent disability to the tune of 40%.

The Apex Court in the case of Mohd. Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain Vs. Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corpn. decided on 9th December, 2022 in Civil Appeal No.9070-9071 of 2022 has observed as under :-
"18.

entities.text: Mohd. Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain Vs. Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corpn
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a well settled position of law that in cases of permanent disablement caused by a motor accident, the claimant is entitled to not just future loss of income, but also future prospects.

It has been reiterated by this Court in multiple instances that "just Rajkumar Pandey vs Sanjay Kumar Singh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57453241/
3 compensation" must be interpreted in such a manner as to place the claimant in the same position as he was before the accident took place."
11.

entities.text: Rajkumar Pandey vs Sanjay Kumar Singh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case of National Insurance Company Limited (Supra), the Apex Court in paragraph 59.8 has directed to award sum in the head of future prospects looking to the nature of employment and age of the victim.

This paragraph is profitably reproduced as under :-
"59.4.

In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component."
12.
In the light of the observation by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the stand case appellant being 36 years of age is entitled for increase of 40% towards future prospects in the total of his income.

13. As regards income of the appellant, learned claims tribunal in paragraph 22 of the impugned award has concluded that in absence of any cogent documentary evidence in the year 2014 notional income of the injured/appellant is taken as Rs.4500/- p.m.

Learned counsel for the appellant has taken objection to this assessment and taking recourse to guidelines issued by the MPSLSA contended that income of the injured should have been taken as Rs.5520/- p.m.
14.

In Sapna and Others vs. Mangilal and Another, 2021 ACJ 957, Coordinate Bench of this Court in para No.8 has held as under:-
"8.Having

entities.text: Sapna and Others vs. Mangilal and Another, 2021 ACJ 957
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: heard the learned counsel for parties and on perusal of the record, it is noticed that the appellant had deposed before the tribunal that the deceased was earning Rs.8,000/- per month, but no document in support of which was produced.

The tribunal had noted that the deceased was about 20 years of age and was a labourer, therefore, considering the minimum wages and dearness allowance for the relevant period, the tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.6000/-.
No notification/circular of the concerned Labour Officer was taken note of by the tribunal while mentioning the daily wages of Rs.6000/-.

The circular dated 7/4/2018 issued by the Labour Officer, Barwani applicable to the period from 01/4/2018 to 30/9/2018 produced by the appellants reveals that the monthly wages on the basis of daily wages along with dearness allowance fixed by the concerned Labour Officer was Rs.7325/-.
Hence, the tribunal ought to have fixed the monthly income on the basis of the said circular."

15. Coordinate Benches of this Court in the cases of Bhim Singh vs. Jagmelsingh in MA No.5350 of 2022 dated 07th July, 2023, Shankar and Others vs Dinesh and Others in MA No.2057 of 2021 dated 08th September, 2023 and Sohanlal and Others vs. Noorasingh and Others in MA No.7014 of 2019 dated 22.08.2023 has also determined income on the basis of minimum wages notified under Rajkumar Pandey vs Sanjay Kumar Singh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57453241/
4 the Minimum Wages Act, 1948.
16.

entities.text: Bhim Singh vs. Jagmelsingh in MA No.5350 of 2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Shankar and Others vs Dinesh and Others in MA No.2057 of 2021 dated 08th September, 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sohanlal and Others vs. Noorasingh and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Rajkumar Pandey vs Sanjay Kumar Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, from principles laid down in above cases, it is evident that Hon'ble Apex Court as well as Coordinate Benches of this Court has consistently determined the income on the basis of Minimum Wages duly notified under Minimum Wages Act, which has been considered while issuing the guidelines of the MPSALSA.
17.

It is correct that as per section 3 & other provisions of Minimum Wages Act, 1948, minimum wages thereunder are fixed & notified for employees employed in an employment specified in the Act, i.e. in respect of scheduled employment under the Act.

But, in view of principles laid down in decisions referred to in preceding paras, in this court's considered opinion, in absence of other evidence on record, to obviate uncertainty & for sake of reasonable uniformity & consistency, it would be just & proper to apply yardstick of Minimum Wages duly notified under Minimum Wages Act, 1948 for determining compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.
18. In view of section 57 of Indian Evidence Act, 1872, judicial notice can be taken of Minimum Wages duly notified under Minimum Wages Act, 1948.
Hence, the same need not to be proved separately.

19. In the light of exposition of law in the above judgments as referred above, the procedure adopted by the learned Claims Tribunal for assessing the income of the injured which is based merely on surmises is incorrect and cannot be approved.
20. The income of the appellant is assessed as Rs.5520/- p.m. as per the guidelines issued by the MPSLSA.

21. In the light of the above discussion as aforesaid the appellant is entitled for the following amount in the head of loss of income :
 Sr. No. Head Compensation  1. Income Rs.5520/- p.
 2. Yearly income Rs.66,240/- 
 3. Future Prospect Rs.26,496/-

4 . Yearly income after adding future Rs.92,736/-
prospect 5. Loss of income (60%) Rs.55,642/-

7. Total loss of income Rs.8,34,630/-
Rajkumar Pandey vs Sanjay Kumar Singh on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57453241/
5 22.

entities.text: Rajkumar Pandey vs Sanjay Kumar Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In addition to the above, the appellant is also entitled for the amount as awarded by the learned claims tribunal in the head of pain and suffering, loss of expectancy of life, treatment and in other heads, if any.

23. The judgments relied upon by the learned counsel for the appellant in support of his contention regarding treating functional disability of the appellant to 100% are distinguishable on factual matrix and therefore of no help.
24. In the judgments relied upon by the learned counsel for the appellant learned tribunal has assessed the functional disability at 100% but it is not so in the instant case.
25. Resultantly, the appeal is party allowed as mentioned hereinabove.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE m/-
